stories.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: CISA has added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including critical flaws in Google Chrome, the Brotli compression library, and multiple versions of PHP. These vulnerabilities are currently being actively exploited in the wild.
stories.why: These flaws are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Chrome to 156.0.8078.73 or later, update Brotli, and patch PHP to the latest secure versions.

stories.title: Adobe Commerce PolyShell Attacks Breach Hundreds of Stores as Brotli Exploit Traffic Emerges
stories.abstract: CISA has added three critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These include flaws in the Google Brotli compression library and two use-after-free vulnerabilities impacting Adobe Commerce and Magento, all of which are currently being actively exploited in the wild.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are under active exploitation and carry high severity scores, posing a significant risk of remote code execution or system compromise.
stories.action: Identify and patch all instances of Adobe Commerce, Magento, and software utilizing the Brotli library immediately.

stories.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
stories.abstract: Researchers revealed that the critical Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability exploited by ShinyHunters is actually a chain of three distinct flaws. The attack sequence begins with a server-side request forgery that leverages the application's inherent trust in its own loopback address to access internal management interfaces.
stories.why: Exploiting chained vulnerabilities allows attackers to bypass perimeter defenses and gain unauthorized access to sensitive internal management systems.
stories.action: Ensure all Oracle PeopleSoft instances are updated to the June 2026 patch release.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz
stories.abstract: Mitsubishi Electric has disclosed multiple critical vulnerabilities across its ICONICS and GENESIS industrial software suites. These flaws allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, bypass authentication, or trigger denial-of-service conditions, potentially leading to unauthorized data manipulation or system destruction.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical industrial control systems, posing significant risks to operational technology environments through potential unauthorized access and system compromise.
stories.action: Review the CISA advisory and apply the latest security patches for your specific software versions.

stories.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
stories.abstract: The state-backed threat actor Volt Typhoon is utilizing a modular framework dubbed Silent Train. This infrastructure leverages a rotating network of compromised edge devices to mask malicious traffic and facilitate zero-day exploits against high-value targets.
stories.why: This technique significantly complicates attribution and network-based detection by blending attack traffic with legitimate activity from compromised consumer hardware.

stories.title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
stories.abstract: A phishing campaign dubbed Skyw4lker is targeting U.S. organizations by exploiting device code authentication flows. Instead of harvesting credentials, attackers leverage legitimate cloud service workflows to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts, effectively bypassing traditional security detection methods.
stories.why: This technique subverts standard MFA and credential-based defenses by abusing trusted authentication mechanisms, making unauthorized access difficult to detect via traditional logs.

stories.title: Serial ransomware crook gets 70 months behind bars for Nefilim, Hive roles
stories.abstract: A Ukrainian national received a 70-month prison sentence for his participation in the Nefilim and Hive ransomware operations. Between 2018 and 2021, he targeted various global organizations, including healthcare facilities, government agencies, and large corporations, to extort victims through data encryption.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing international legal efforts to dismantle ransomware affiliate networks and hold individual threat actors accountable for their criminal activities.

stories.title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical vulnerability affecting the Brotli compression library, often referred to as Node2Shell, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Threat actors are actively leveraging this flaw, which impacts a significant portion of web infrastructure, to conduct malicious operations.
stories.why: The widespread use of the affected library across web applications creates a massive attack surface for remote code execution.
stories.action: Identify and patch systems utilizing vulnerable versions of the Brotli compression library immediately.

stories.title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
stories.abstract: Tailscale released version 1.104.4 to address multiple vulnerabilities in its SSH implementation. These flaws allow a compromised device within a Tailscale network to escalate privileges and gain root access on other reachable servers if SSH port forwarding is enabled.
stories.why: Exploitation enables lateral movement and full system compromise across internal infrastructure, bypassing standard access controls for authenticated network participants.
stories.action: Update Tailscale to version 1.104.4 or later immediately.

stories.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell under attack as researchers clock successful exploits
stories.abstract: CISA has officially added two critical PHP vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Security researchers have confirmed that threat actors are actively leveraging these flaws to gain unauthorized remote shell access on vulnerable systems.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical PHP vulnerabilities poses a significant risk of remote code execution and full server compromise.
stories.action: Identify and patch all PHP instances to the latest secure versions immediately.

stories.title: PHP2Shell Attack Roots 25 Servers, Breaches U.S. Government-Affiliated Network
stories.abstract: A China-linked threat actor utilized PHP2Shell vulnerabilities alongside a kernel privilege escalation exploit to compromise 25 servers, including a network affiliated with the U.S. government. The campaign reportedly incorporated AI-assisted techniques to facilitate the intrusion.
stories.why: The combination of web-shell deployment and kernel-level exploitation demonstrates a sophisticated, multi-stage attack path capable of achieving full system persistence.

stories.title: Adobe Fixes 8 Critical Campaign Classic Flaws Allowing Code Execution and Security Bypass
stories.abstract: Adobe patched eight critical vulnerabilities in Campaign Classic, including a high-severity code injection flaw. These security gaps could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, or bypass existing security controls within the platform.
stories.why: Critical remote code execution flaws in enterprise campaign management software provide attackers with a direct path to internal network compromise.
stories.action: Update Adobe Campaign Classic to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: WatchGuard security advisory (AV26-1094)
stories.abstract: WatchGuard has disclosed security vulnerabilities impacting Fireware OS and the Mobile VPN with SSL client. Administrators should review the official advisory to determine if their current deployments are affected and identify the necessary remediation steps for their specific environment.
stories.why: Unpatched network security appliances are frequent targets for initial access and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Review the WatchGuard advisory and apply updates for Fireware OS and Mobile VPN with SSL.

stories.title: Progress security advisory (AV26-1098)
stories.abstract: Progress has disclosed a resource consumption vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-118035, affecting Telerik Document Processing Libraries. The flaw impacts versions prior to 2026.3.1027, potentially allowing attackers to exhaust system resources through malicious document processing.
stories.why: Uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerabilities can lead to denial-of-service conditions, disrupting critical business applications that rely on Telerik libraries.
stories.action: Update Telerik Document Processing Libraries to version 2026.3.1027 or later.

stories.title: Oracle Corporation security advisory (AV26-1071) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Oracle has issued an updated security advisory detailing vulnerabilities across a broad range of its software products, including various JD Edwards EnterpriseOne modules, MySQL components, and several Oracle Agile and identity management platforms.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities affect critical database and enterprise management infrastructure, potentially exposing sensitive business data to unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Review the Oracle advisory and apply the latest security patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: Tanium security advisory (AV26-1097)
stories.abstract: Tanium released a security advisory addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including Certificate Manager, Endpoint Configuration Toolset, Enforce, Provision, and Threat Response. Users should review the specific version requirements to determine if their current deployments are affected by these security gaps.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in endpoint management platforms can provide attackers with elevated access or persistence across an entire enterprise network.
stories.action: Update Tanium modules to the versions specified in advisory AV26-1097.

stories.title: Veeam security advisory (AV26-1096)
stories.abstract: Veeam has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its product suite, including Veeam Agent for Linux, Backup and Replication, Backup for Microsoft 365, and Veeam ONE. Administrators should verify their current versions against the latest patches provided by the vendor.
stories.why: Unpatched backup infrastructure is a high-value target for ransomware actors seeking to disable recovery capabilities and exfiltrate sensitive data.
stories.action: Update Veeam products to the latest versions specified in the vendor security advisory.

stories.title: TeamViewer security advisory (AV26-1093)
stories.abstract: TeamViewer has released security updates addressing vulnerabilities across its Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android client applications. Users running versions prior to 15.83 on desktop platforms or 15.8.3 on Android are affected and should upgrade to the latest releases immediately.
stories.why: Remote access software is a high-value target for attackers; unpatched vulnerabilities can lead to unauthorized system control and persistence.
stories.action: Update TeamViewer clients to version 15.83 or later.

stories.title: Adobe security advisory (AV26-1092)
stories.abstract: Adobe has released a series of security updates addressing vulnerabilities across several products, including Substance 3D Painter, Creative Cloud Desktop, Campaign Classic, and Adobe Connect. These patches follow a broader set of fixes issued earlier this year for various creative and commerce tools.
stories.why: Unpatched Adobe software frequently serves as an initial access vector for attackers targeting enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update Substance 3D Painter, Creative Cloud, Campaign Classic, and Adobe Connect to the latest versions.

stories.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
stories.abstract: Sony Network Communications disclosed a security incident involving the unauthorized access of a database. The breach impacted roughly 2.5 million current and former customers, exposing sensitive personal information stored within the subsidiary's systems.
stories.why: Large-scale exposure of PII increases the risk of targeted phishing and identity theft campaigns against the affected user base.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
stories.abstract: State-sponsored actors from China compromised two servers belonging to a US government-affiliated entity. The attackers achieved root access by chaining the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to infiltrate the organization's firewall infrastructure.
stories.why: This demonstrates sophisticated exploitation of edge devices to gain persistent access to sensitive government networks.

stories.title: EPICS Base
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in EPICS Base versions 7.0.10 and earlier, including integer overflows and type confusion, could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, corrupt memory, or trigger denial-of-service conditions within industrial control environments.
stories.why: These flaws impact critical infrastructure systems, potentially allowing unauthorized remote code execution or system disruption.
stories.action: Update EPICS Base to a version beyond 7.0.10.

stories.title: Microsoft releases out-of-band Windows fixes with certificate updates
stories.abstract: Microsoft issued out-of-band updates for Windows to revoke trust in specific eMudhra certificate authority keys. This action mitigates risks associated with compromised certificates that could otherwise be leveraged for malicious authentication or traffic interception.
stories.why: Compromised CA keys allow attackers to forge trusted digital signatures, potentially enabling malware distribution or man-in-the-middle attacks.
stories.action: Install the latest Windows out-of-band security updates.

stories.title: Unwrapping Retail Peak Season Cyber Threats
stories.abstract: Unit 42 has released a seasonal advisory highlighting elevated cyber risks for the retail sector. The report emphasizes threats ranging from ransomware deployments to automated AI-driven attacks, urging organizations to bolster their defensive posture to protect operational integrity and consumer data during high-traffic periods.
stories.why: Retailers face increased financial and reputational risk during peak shopping windows, making them prime targets for extortion and credential harvesting campaigns.

stories.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
stories.abstract: Researchers identified three vulnerabilities in the GoAhead embedded web server. The flaws allow revoked certificates to bypass authentication and potentially expose encrypted traffic, specifically affecting configurations that utilize OpenSSL for mutual TLS authentication.
stories.why: The server is widely deployed in hundreds of millions of IoT and embedded devices, creating a massive, difficult-to-patch attack surface.

stories.title: Yet Another ClickFix Campaign, (Wed, Oct 28th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center reports on a new wave of ClickFix-style social engineering campaigns. These attacks leverage deceptive browser prompts to trick users into executing malicious PowerShell scripts, often disguised as troubleshooting steps for common software errors.
stories.why: This technique bypasses traditional endpoint defenses by manipulating users into manually executing obfuscated code, highlighting a persistent gap in human-centric security controls.

stories.title: Moldova investigates possible foreign involvement in major government cyberattack
stories.abstract: Moldovan officials are investigating a significant cyberattack against state digital infrastructure. Prime Minister Vasile Tofan indicated the breach may be part of a larger, coordinated campaign aimed at compromising government systems and the personal information of the country's citizens.
stories.why: State-sponsored campaigns targeting national infrastructure often signal evolving geopolitical tensions and sophisticated persistent threats against government data repositories.

stories.title: Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach
123 Reg discloses 'AI cyberattack' on customer data, suspects China nexus
stories.abstract: Web host 123 Reg reported a data breach involving unauthorized access to customer information. The company suspects the intrusion was orchestrated by a sophisticated threat actor potentially linked to the ARTEX campaign previously observed targeting South Korean financial institutions.
stories.why: The potential involvement of advanced persistent threats suggests a high-capability adversary targeting infrastructure providers for data exfiltration or supply chain positioning.

stories.title: UNM Health ransomware attack disrupts patient care, surgeries
stories.abstract: The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center is managing significant system outages following a cyberattack. The incident has forced the organization to postpone surgeries and disrupt academic operations as they work to restore affected infrastructure.
stories.why: Healthcare providers remain high-value targets for ransomware, often resulting in critical service degradation and potential exposure of sensitive patient health information.

stories.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in the Microsoft Authenticator app for Android allowed unauthorized applications to masquerade as trusted services like Teams. This flaw enabled attackers to intercept and steal authentication tokens associated with enterprise user accounts without requiring any specific device permissions.
stories.why: Token theft bypasses traditional credentials, potentially granting attackers persistent access to sensitive corporate environments and cloud resources.
stories.action: Update Microsoft Authenticator for Android to version 6.2606.4246 or later.

stories.title: In-the-Wild Attack Abuses AI Agents' Trust in Markdown
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a novel prompt injection method targeting AI coding assistants. By manipulating local Markdown files, attackers can trick agents into executing unauthorized commands, effectively turning passive documentation into a vector for malicious system-level actions.
stories.why: This highlights a critical supply chain risk where AI agents blindly trust local configuration or instruction files, leading to potential remote code execution.

stories.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
stories.abstract: GMO Group has advised Onamae Desktop Cloud users to disconnect their machines from the internet and power them down. This follows a security breach where an attacker threatened to deploy ransomware against the company's infrastructure today.
stories.why: Cloud service providers are high-value targets for ransomware actors, potentially exposing customer data and virtualized environments to encryption or exfiltration.
stories.action: Disconnect affected systems from the network and power them down immediately.

stories.title: [Control systems] Hitachi security advisory (AV26-1091)
stories.abstract: Hitachi has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting several versions of its HiRDB server software and various JP1 management tools. Additionally, the TRO600 series firmware requires updates to address security flaws found in versions prior to 9.2.2.1.
stories.why: Unpatched industrial and management software can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical infrastructure and enterprise job scheduling environments.
stories.action: Review Hitachi security advisory AV26-1091 and apply available patches for affected HiRDB, JP1, and TRO600 products.

stories.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
stories.abstract: Recent analysis of the PHP2Shell exploit highlights that rapid vulnerability exploitation often outpaces patching cycles. Security experts emphasize that restricting the permissions of service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is essential to containing the impact of a successful breach.
stories.why: It underscores that defense-in-depth and principle of least privilege are more effective at limiting blast radius than relying solely on rapid patching.

stories.title: Hackers hijack Convertr analytics script to steal payment card data
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised a shared analytics script hosted by Convertr, enabling them to intercept and exfiltrate customer payment information during the checkout process on e-commerce sites utilizing the platform.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting third-party scripts remain a highly effective method for bypassing perimeter defenses and harvesting sensitive financial data at scale.

stories.title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively targeting critical network appliances, including VPNs and firewalls, by leveraging PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. These flaws specifically compromise web-based management interfaces, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized control over essential infrastructure components.
stories.why: Compromised management interfaces provide attackers with full administrative access to network perimeters, facilitating lateral movement and persistent data exfiltration.
stories.action: Audit and restrict access to web management interfaces for all network appliances.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Moxa security advisory (AV26-1089)
stories.abstract: Moxa has disclosed three vulnerabilities affecting the Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client) version 4.2.0 and earlier, as well as all firmware versions of the OnCell G3150A-LTE series. Users should review the manufacturer's advisory for remediation details.
stories.why: These flaws impact industrial remote access and cellular gateway hardware, potentially allowing unauthorized control or access to critical operational technology environments.
stories.action: Review the Moxa security advisory and apply available firmware or software updates.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Wednesday, October 28th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10154, (Wed, Oct 28th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for October 28, 2026, provides a daily summary of current cybersecurity trends, emerging threats, and technical analysis relevant to security practitioners monitoring the global threat landscape.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat intelligence helps security teams identify patterns and prioritize defensive measures against evolving attack vectors.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
stories.abstract: Microsoft is pushing Entra ID administrators to transition users toward phishing-resistant passkeys. This initiative aims to phase out SMS and voice-based multi-factor authentication methods, which are scheduled for complete retirement by February 2027.
stories.why: SMS and voice authentication are vulnerable to interception and social engineering; moving to passkeys significantly improves identity security posture.
stories.action: Begin planning and testing the migration from SMS and voice MFA to passkeys.

stories.title: Attacker Relentlessly Scans for Credentials by Impersonating AI Bots
stories.abstract: Threat actors are masquerading as legitimate AI crawlers from major companies like OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic. By mimicking these automated agents, attackers are scanning public-facing infrastructure to identify and harvest exposed credentials or sensitive data.
stories.why: Attackers are exploiting the trust organizations place in AI web scrapers to bypass standard security filters and gain unauthorized access.
stories.action: Update firewall and WAF rules to verify the authenticity of incoming AI bot traffic.

stories.title: 'Aokigahara' Stealer Targets 'Developer Keyrings' & AI Assistants
stories.abstract: A new information-stealing malware dubbed Aokigahara is actively targeting developer environments. The threat focuses on harvesting credentials from local keyrings and intercepting active sessions within AI-powered coding assistants to exfiltrate sensitive business data and proprietary infrastructure access.
stories.why: It signals a shift in malware tactics toward compromising AI-integrated development workflows to gain deeper access to corporate intellectual property.

stories.title: External Teams Chats Anchor 15-Minute Malware Delivery
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging external Microsoft Teams chat invitations to conduct a massive social engineering campaign. The strategy involves flooding targets with notifications to facilitate malware delivery, with researchers suspecting links to the Black Basta ransomware syndicate.
stories.why: This technique bypasses traditional email filters by utilizing trusted communication platforms to deliver malicious payloads directly to corporate users.

stories.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning the internet to identify and exploit unpatched Oracle E-Business Suite instances. This activity targets a recently disclosed critical vulnerability, indicating that attackers are moving quickly to weaponize the flaw against vulnerable enterprise environments.
stories.why: Active exploitation attempts against critical business software increase the risk of unauthorized access and potential data breaches for organizations running EBS.
stories.action: Apply the latest Oracle security patches to all E-Business Suite installations immediately.

stories.title: Google to Allow One-Tap Android App Installs From Approved Third-Party Stores Outside U.S.
stories.abstract: Google is enabling approved third-party Android app stores to bypass standard installation prompts and perform background updates. To participate, these stores must submit their entire software catalogs to Google for continuous malware analysis and undergo rigorous identity verification processes.
stories.why: This expands the attack surface for mobile devices by integrating third-party distribution channels directly into the operating system's automated update and installation flows.

stories.title: South Korea’s financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks
stories.abstract: Financial institutions across South Korea are experiencing a new surge of cyberattacks. Security analysts suggest these incidents underscore an increasing threat landscape in Asia, specifically driven by the integration of artificial intelligence tools into malicious hacking operations.
stories.why: The shift toward AI-enhanced cyberattacks signals a potential escalation in the sophistication and speed of threats targeting critical financial infrastructure.

stories.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
European digital rights nonprofit noyb sues Scale AI for ‘invasive’ worker surveillance
stories.abstract: The digital rights organization noyb has filed a lawsuit against Scale AI, alleging the company subjects its remote workforce to excessive surveillance. The complaint claims the platform captures frequent screenshots and keystroke data, effectively creating comprehensive video logs of employees' daily activities.
stories.why: This highlights growing privacy concerns regarding invasive employee monitoring tools and the potential for data misuse within AI training supply chains.

stories.title: From industry concern to practical action: the value of working with regulators
stories.abstract: The NCSC and the Financial Conduct Authority have established a collaborative framework for financial institutions to exchange threat intelligence. This initiative aims to improve collective defense mechanisms while ensuring that information sharing remains compliant with market integrity and regulatory standards.
stories.why: Standardized information sharing protocols reduce friction for security teams when reporting incidents or collaborating on threat intelligence within highly regulated financial sectors.

stories.title: UK to look at making software companies liable for cyber breaches
stories.abstract: The British government is evaluating a policy shift that could hold software vendors legally accountable for security failures. This proposal marks a significant departure from the nation's current reliance on voluntary security standards and industry self-regulation.
stories.why: Legislative changes regarding vendor liability could fundamentally alter software procurement, risk management, and legal exposure for organizations operating in the UK.

stories.title: Belarusian hackers increasingly acting as proxies for Russia amid war in Ukraine
stories.abstract: Security researchers have observed Belarusian threat actors intensifying their alignment with Russian strategic objectives regarding the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. These groups are increasingly functioning as operational proxies to support Russian cyber activities.
stories.why: The integration of Belarusian hacking collectives into Russian state-sponsored campaigns expands the threat surface and complicates attribution for regional cyber operations.

stories.title: Day 2 of canceled classes at University of New Mexico after Health Sciences Center cyberattack
Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
ICE Is Running One of the Largest Anti-Left Surveillance Operations in US History
Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
Fake PS5 emulators on GitHub are spreading password-stealing malware
Chrome’s AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms
